models.name: Model A: CT-mapped femur with detailed cemented resurfacing construct
models.what_it_computes: Implicit quasi-static stress/strain fields, interface contact tractions, and compartmental load transfer in a patient-average femur with heterogeneous elastic properties and an explicit cement mantle

models.name: Model B: Surrogate femur with homogenized cortical/trabecular shells
models.what_it_computes: Implicit quasi-static stress/strain fields and load sharing using a geometry-calibrated composite femur, homogeneous orthotropic properties, and simplified cement-implant interface

mechanisms.name: Femoral neck load transfer during level walking
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Alters stress pathways through the calcar and superior neck; aberrant redistribution can elevate fracture risk or compromise construct longevity

mechanisms.name: Proximal femoral stress shielding during stair ascent
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Reduced mechanical stimulus in Gruen-like proximal regions can drive bone resorption, threatening fixation and leading to revision

deviation.detail: Each credibility factor is scored per model–mechanism pair on a 0–12 Assurance Index, where 0–3 = low, 4–8 = moderate, and 9–12 = high assurance; category boundaries are used throughout without qualification

findings.mechanism: Femoral neck load transfer during level walking
spans: Model A is a high-fidelity construct coupling a CT-mapped, heterogeneous femur to an explicit cement mantle and a cobalt-chromium cap with porous backing.

As part of establishing the adequacy of structural idealiza-tions for the intended decision, we observe that the explicit representation of the cement mantle and cohesive bone–cement behavior in Model A, together with CT-based heterogeneity and porous backing stiffness, reproduces the key mechanical discontinuities and stiffness transitions expected to govern neck load flow and proximal stimulus; in contrast, the composite-layer representation in Model B accelerates solution time but blurs stress gradients at the cement–bone interface, reducing local fidelity while preserving bulk bending response.
findings.span: Model A is a high-fidelity construct coupling a CT-mapped, heterogeneous femur to an explicit cement mantle and a cobalt-chromium cap with porous backing.

findings.mechanism: Femoral neck load transfer during level walking
spans: Under these settings, the change in calcar strain for Model A was 0.6 percent (walking) and 0.9 percent (stair ascent); for Model B, the changes were 0.4 percent and 0.6 percent.
Contact stabilization energy was monitored and remained below 0.4 percent of total strain energy across all runs.
